Let \(P=(x,y)\). Then
\[
\overrightarrow{F_1P}=(x+\sqrt3,y),\qquad \overrightarrow{PF_2}=(\sqrt3-x,-y).
\]
Since \(F_1P\perp PF_2\),
\[
(x+\sqrt3)(\sqrt3-x)+y(-y)=0
\]
\[
3-x^2-y^2=0 \implies x^2+y^2=3.
\]
Also \(P\) lies on
\[
\frac{x^2}{4}+y^2=1.
\]
Solving with \(x^2+y^2=3\):
\[
\frac{x^2}{4}+(3-x^2)=1 \implies x^2=\frac83,\quad y^2=\frac13.
\]
Thus the height from \(P\) to \(F_1F_2\) is
\[
|y|=\frac1{\sqrt3}.
\]
The base is
\[
F_1F_2=2\sqrt3.
\]
So the area is
\[
\frac12\cdot 2\sqrt3\cdot \frac1{\sqrt3}=1.
\]
\[
\boxed{1}
\]
